title_content.content: Palladium-Catalyzed Intermolecular [5+ 2] Cycloaddition: Highly Regioselective Synthesis of Allene-Containing 2- Benzoxepines

paragraph_content.content: Bingyu Shen,<sup>[a,</sup> <sup>b]</sup> Aimei Yang,<sup>[b]</sup> Xihong Lu,<sup>[a]</sup> Zhijun Xin,*<sup>[a]</sup> and Xuehu Li*<sup>[a]</sup>

Palladium-catalyzed intermolecular [5 + 2] cycloaddition of propargylic carbonates with benzyl allenyl ethers has been developed for the synthesis of allene-containing 2-benzoxepines. The reaction proceeds by a pathway involving decarbox-

As representative seven-membered oxygen-containing heterocycles, 2-benzoxepines represent a significant structural motif in numerous natural products and synthetic pharmaceuticals that exhibit a wide range of biological and physiological activities (Figure 1).<sup>[1]</sup> For example, Doxepin demonstrates both antidepressant and sedative-hypnotic effects,<sup>[2]</sup> Obtuanhydride displays antifungal activity,<sup>[3]</sup> whereas xylarinols A has proven to inhibit the activity of yeast α-glucosidase.<sup>[4]</sup> In view of the importance of 2-benzoxepines, the establishment of efficient and straightforward construction methods for synthesizing these scaffolds has attracted considerable attention from the organic synthesis community.<sup>[5]</sup>

In the past decades, tremendous advances have been achieved in synthetic methods for the construction of 2- benzoxepine skeletons, such as transannular macrocyclization via intramolecular B-alkyl Suzuki reaction,<sup>[6]</sup> tandem
\mathsf { S } _ { \mathsf { N } } 2

paragraph_content.content: Intermolecular cycloadditions of allenes derivatives via palladium-catalyzed have been discovered to efficiently integrate various structural fragments while maintaining high atom and step economy. Consequently, this method offers straightforward and effective approaches for the synthesis of heterocycles.<sup>[12]</sup> Remarkably, Ma et al. employed the aforementioned strategy to develop a series of novel methods for synthesizing complex six-membered oxygen-containing<sup>[13]</sup> and eight-membered nitrogen-containing<sup>[14]</sup> heterocycles, utilizing allene derivatives and propargylic carbonates as starting materials. However, the synthesis of seven-membered hetero cycles has not been reported to date. Inspired by these findings, we envisioned a strategy for the construction of 2-benzoxepine skeletons through decarboxylation/cycloaddition of propargylic carbonates with benzyl allenyl ethers. Herein, we present our efforts on Pd(0)-catalyzed intermolecular [5 + 2] cycloaddition, which provides an ideal and concise approach for synthesizing functionalized 2-benzoxepine frameworks Scheme 1.

Subsequently, we evaluated the different types of ligands necessary for the reaction (entries 6–13), such as monodentate phosphine ligands, bidentate phosphine ligands and boron reagents. The results revealed that monodentate phosphine ligands exhibited superior performance compared to both bidentate phosphine ligands and boron reagents. Notably, when 2-(diphenylphosphino) pyridine (L1) was employed as the ligand the yield of the target product increased to 66 % (entry 9). With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we explored the scope and generality of the cyclization reaction through a systematic investigation of the electronic nature of the substituents on substrates 2 under the optimal conditions (Table 2). The yield of the para-methoxy-substituted product 3 b was 62 %, which was slightly lower than that of product 3a. Additionally, the yield of the meta-methoxy-substituted analogue 3 c further decreased to 55%. As the number of methoxy substituent groups on the benzene ring of substrates 2 increased, the yields of the corresponding multi-methoxysubstituted products 3 d and 3 e exhibited a downward trend. The substrate 2 containing dioxygen substituent demonstrated tolerance and afforded the desired cyclization product 3 f in 54 % yield. Notably, the naphthylmethyl allenyl ether was successfully converted into 3 g, achieving a yield of 72 %, which surpassed that of 3 a. The increase in yield may be attributed to the electron effects of the naphthalene ring. Next, we investigated the reactivity of benzyl allenyl ethers with fluorine or chlorine substituents, successfully obtaining the target products 3 h and 3 i in 43% and 55% yields, respectively. However, the iodine-substituted substrate 2j did not give the target product, which could be primarily attributed to the oxidative insertion of Pd into the C�I bond, leading to an unintended coupling reaction.<sup>[15]</sup> To our surprise, substrates 2 containing a strong EWG (CN,
{ \mathsf { C F } } _ { 3 } )
also furnished the expected products 3 k and 3 l in satisfactory yields. In summary, substrates 2 bearing EDG or EWG are well tolerated, delivering corresponding products in moderate to good yields.

To further evaluate the robustness of the methodology, the reactivity of dioxygen-substituted propargylic carbonate 1 b and diverse benzyl allenyl ethers 2 was investigated (Table 3). The catalytic system similarly demonstrated tolerance to the reaction of 1 b with benzyl allenyl ethers 2 which were substituted with methoxyl, fluorine, chlorine, trifluoromethyl and cyano groups, as well as with naphthylmethyl allenyl ether, yielding 2-benzoxepines in 35% to 60% (4a–4h). A comparison of the yields of 3a and 4a, 3b and
{ \mathfrak { 4 } } \mathbf { b } ,

3d and 4c, 3g and 4d, 3 h and 4e, 3 i and 4 f, 3 k and 4 g, as well as 3 l and 4 h revealed that, when reacting with the same benzyl allenyl ether 2, the yields of 2-benzoxepines synthesized from substrate 1 b were lower than those synthesized from substrate 1 a. This observation indicated that the presence of electron-withdrawing substituents on the benzene ring of substrates 1 was not favorable for the reaction. As anticipated, benzyl allenyl ethers with a methyl substituent at the ortho or para position of the allenyl ether group underwent transformations smoothly, generating the corresponding products in 57 % and 58% yields, respectively (4 i and 4j). However, due to steric hindrance, the yield of the isopropyl-substituted product 4 k was limited to only 44%.

Following the above experiments, we devoted our attention to various leaving groups on propargylic carbonates (Table 4). The reactions involving propargyl ethyl carbonate 1 c and propargyl benzyl carbonate 1d demonstrated good compatibility and yielded acceptable results under the tested conditions (entries 1 and 2). In contrast, propargyl phosphate 1 e exhibited lower reactivity, potentially due to the reduced leaving ability of phosphate compared to that of the aforementioned carbonates (entry 3).

Based on previous studies<sup>[13]</sup> and experimental results, a plausible mechanism for the formation of functionalized 2- benzoxepine scaffolds is depicted in Scheme 2. Initially, oxidative addition of 1 a with catalytically active palladium(0) leads to afford allenylpalladium intermediate
Subsequently, species 5 undergoes highly regioselective intermolecular insertion of the nonterminal
\mathsf { C } { = } \mathsf { C }
bond on the allene moiety in 2a to generate allylpalladium intermediate

In the presence of base, intermediate 6 is converted to intermediate 7. Finally, the key intermediate 7 undergoes regioselective intramolecular nucleophilic attack to form seven-membered ring product 3 a and regenerate the catalytically active palladium (0).<sup>[18]</sup> Additionally, electronic effects of the benzyloxy group in substrates 2 may be the key controlling factor that produces regioselectivity.
